- `data.credits.18220c7d`: The memory SETTLE remembers with: an address space of 2^n corners, a few thousand hard locations scattered in it at random, a write that adds to the counters of every location near the address, and a read that lets those locations vote.

- `data.credits.2664e402`: The update every sweep runs: one thing at a time flips to yes with probability (1 + tanh(beta I)) / 2, given its neighbours.

- `data.descend.2abd50f6`: c, the bias
- `data.descend.4743368b`: a real fit (logistic loss of 20 points)
- `data.descend.4767ff0d`: E = (x^2 - 1)^2 - 0.35 x + y^2: a shallow well on the left, a deeper one on the right, a hill of about 1 between. Started on the left, gradient descent stays left; heat carries walkers over the hill; cooling slowly leaves most of them in the deeper well.
- `data.descend.4a44986f`: the banana (a curved valley)
- `data.descend.69a6c057`: the bowl (the springs above)
- `data.descend.82b474d9`: two wells (a hill between)
- `data.descend.9efb254a`: w, the slope
- `data.descend.e81a2566`: E = (1 - x)^2 + 4 (y - x^2)^2: a long curved valley floor. Gradient descent zigzags down the steep walls, then crawls along the floor to (1, 1).
- `data.descend.ec38f461`: E = x.A.x/2 - b.x with A = [[3, 1], [1, 2]], b = [1, 1]: the NUMBERS springs. One valley, so gradient descent finds it, and the hot cloud is a Gaussian with covariance T A^-1.
- `data.descend.effcbeee`: E(w, c) = sum over 20 examples of [log(1 + e^z) - y z], z = w x + c, plus (w^2 + c^2)/18: logistic regression with a prior of sd 3. At T = 1 the cloud is the Bayesian posterior over the slope w and the bias c.

- `data.glossary.0a4bff89`: The word stored and read back. In SETTLE's autoassociative memories the data word is the pattern itself.
- `data.glossary.2ded83e4`: Sampling: re-tossing one thing at a time so that each arrangement turns up with probability proportional to exp(-energy / temperature).
- `data.glossary.3a0d6bae`: The Model Context Protocol: a client such as Claude Code starts a server and calls the tools it registers.
- `data.glossary.3f90fdc4`: The number of bit positions in which two words differ.
- `data.glossary.41a3462a`: How far a read-address can be from a stored word and still converge to it under iterated reads.
- `data.glossary.5645a572`: What one run block holds: the held things, the samples drawn and the counts that show and ask report.
- `data.glossary.59655103`: A thing's own preference, a real number h. leans: :yes, by: b adds +b to it.
- `data.glossary.5fc7f6b2`: The address you read at. SETTLE says read because the statement is s.read.
- `data.glossary.68156c98`: One yes or no value for every thing of a model at once.
- `data.glossary.7faf967d`: How settle-mcp talks to its client: messages on the process’s input and output, no network port.
- `data.glossary.8926dd78`: A named yes/no variable of a model. In any arrangement its value is yes (+1) or no (-1).
- `data.glossary.8a00a85f`: The address a word is stored at.
- `data.glossary.8b2daade`: The integer counters each hard-location keeps, one per bit of the data word. A write adds +1 or -1 to each.
- `data.glossary.9f70dfe7`: The memory locations that are built, each with a fixed random address.
- `data.glossary.a3fa9249`: A probabilistic bit: a coin that comes up +1 or -1 with a chance set by the push on it.
- `data.glossary.a9db0913`: The fraction of the read-address's bits flipped at random before the read. address-noise: 0.2 flips a fifth of them.
- `data.glossary.c8235994`: A number J between two things. A positive pull makes them agree, a negative pull (a push) makes them disagree.
- `data.glossary.cf80f731`: The fraction of hard-locations one address activates. SETTLE derives the activation-radius from it.
- `data.glossary.d1f23b3d`: The most times a read uses its own result as the next read-address. The read stops early when the result stops changing.
- `data.glossary.d8d64d9c`: Pentti Kanerva's memory (1988): long binary words are written to the many hard locations near their address and read back by a vote of the locations near a read-address.
- `data.glossary.db06198c`: How much the samples ignore the energy. Hot: nearly random. Cold: nearly always the calmest arrangement.
- `data.glossary.e6526c96`: The number of bits in an address and in a data word. SETTLE uses one length for both.
- `data.glossary.ea4ece08`: Settling while the temperature steps down, so the arrangement ends near the lowest energy.
- `data.glossary.f66590dc`: A setup call that runs nothing and returns every command with a plan id; the second call must repeat that id.
- `data.glossary.f7917891`: The hard-locations within the activation-radius of an address.
- `data.glossary.f9b0038b`: The Hamming distance within which a hard-location is activated by an address.
- `data.glossary.fe37f969`: A number for each arrangement: minus the leans times the values, minus the pulls times the paired values. Low energy is likely.

- `data.herocontrols.9a8a9a34`: Everything keeps one beat. The light, the sound, the picture's 500 ms frames and the music's bar lines all count from the page's one master clock. The light draws a frame bright or dark by where that frame falls on the master beat, drops a frame the screen missed rather than catching up, and never flashes twice in one cycle. The sound starts on a master tick, so a 40 Hz binaural beat and the light cross their starts together.

- `data.herocontrols.b419b998`: A 60 Hz screen cannot show 40 Hz at all: a cycle there is a whole number of frames, so the rates it draws exactly are 30 Hz (one frame lit, one dark), 15 Hz, 10 Hz and slower. Asked for 40 Hz, it draws an uneven pattern the eye reads mostly as 20 Hz. So on a display below 100 frames a second the light runs the nearest exact rate and says so: 30 Hz at 60, 36 at 72, 37.5 at 75, 45 at 90.

- `data.kanerva.1500130b`: At Kanerva's 1988 operating point (1,000-bit words, a million hard locations, ten thousand stored patterns) the critical distance, the farthest a read-address can start and still come back to its pattern, measured 204.3 bits: above the 188 read from Kanerva's own figure and above our own signal-to-noise estimate of 165.
- `data.kanerva.16a69249`: The memory can say "I never stored that"
- `data.kanerva.1e932ea1`: A soft edge turns SDM into attention
- `data.kanerva.21e866df`: Kanerva's own critical distance, rebuilt at a million hard locations
- `data.kanerva.5117afe7`: At equal memory, SDM holds far more than a Hopfield net
- `data.kanerva.5f4cabcc`: With a read-address that has 10% of its bits wrong, the number of patterns the memory recalls in 90% of reads rises almost in proportion to the number of hard locations, from 2,000 hard locations to a million.
- `data.kanerva.819e340b`: With the memory of a million 256-bit hard locations, a Hopfield net of the same size recalls 100 patterns at 10% address-noise; SDM read by address recalls 20,000, and SDM read by content (the top-k rows that match the read-address) 70,000.
- `data.kanerva.8e6633b3`: Capacity grows with the number of hard locations
- `data.kanerva.aba349fa`: A read that moves a random read-address a long way is refused (rule R: travel above a threshold set by how many patterns are stored); where random read-addresses settle onto stored patterns, this refusal matches a memory that sees every pattern, at no cost to recall up to 30% address-noise.
- `data.kanerva.c540b8fd`: Built from p-bits with a soft cut-off, the memory reads like a softmax attention over its stored patterns, agreeing on 93 to 96% of reads where recall works, but holding fewer patterns than the ideal kernel or softmax.

- `docs.top.count.tests.what`: #[test] functions in src/ and tests/
- `docs.top.counts`: {examples} example programs in docs/examples/, every one run and compared by cargo test --release; {tests} test functions in the crate. Recount: {re1} and {re2}.
- `docs.top.counts.unknown`: This build had no copy of the crate beside it, so it did not count the examples or the tests. Count them in a clone: {re1} and {re2}.
- `docs.top.defaults.h`: Five defaults, each one measured
- `docs.top.defaults.lead`: A program that names none of these options gets the setting that measured better. Each old default is still there as an option. The changelog has the full entry.
- `docs.top.json.err`: This program pulls on a thing it never declared:
- `docs.top.json.h`: Answers as JSON
- `docs.top.json.lead`: Put --json before the program and settle prints one JSON object: the lines, or the error with its line and column. An editor or an MCP server reads it this way. The exit status stays the same: 0, or 2 for an error.
- `docs.top.knife1`: Every answer is a count over samples, so it is an estimate. The same seed gives the same estimate every run.
- `docs.top.knife2`: A failing line prints one message and exits with status 2, and the lines before it print nothing.
- `docs.top.knife3`: anneal keeps the calmest arrangement it visits, which is a search, not a proof. On a 9x9 sudoku with 30 givens it reaches a valid grid in 35% of 50 seeds at 2,000 sweeps and 94% at 50,000.
- `docs.top.knives.h`: Where it breaks is written down
- `docs.top.rust.h`: The same program, in Rust
- `docs.top.rust.lead`: The core statements have a second face for Rust: the builder, Model::build(). Its methods are the words of the program, and it prints the same lines. A test compiles this file as written. The builder face has the rest.
- `docs.top.sell.h`: Bayes falls out of a count
- `docs.top.sell.lead`: Three things lean no. Two pulls say a burglary or an earthquake sets the alarm off, and one push says the two causes compete. Hold the alarm at yes and the burglary rises to 56.5%. Hold the earthquake at yes as well and it falls to 26.8%. Nobody wrote a rule for that. The whole program, with all three questions, is [in the cookbook](#condition-on-evidence).
- `docs.top.step1`: clone it and build it
- `docs.top.step1.note`: Always the release build: the debug build runs the same coin flips many times slower.
- `docs.top.step2.first`: run your first settle
- `docs.top.step3.note`: The sdm statements are KANERVA’s memory, mounted in SETTLE. The tour reads this program line by line, and KANERVA shows the same memory as a Rust builder and a .kanerva file.
- `docs.top.step3.sdm`: write your first sdm statement

## epics

- `epics.compose.col.data`: continued on
- `epics.compose.col.epics`: held-out epic lines (bpb)
- `epics.compose.col.fw`: FineWeb-Edu TEST (bpb)
- `epics.compose.col.run`: run
- `epics.compose.cue`: cue
- `epics.compose.data.base`: nothing more (the starting model, 300M FineWeb-Edu tokens)
- `epics.compose.data.ep12`: 12M tokens of the epics
- `epics.compose.data.fw12`: 12M tokens of FineWeb-Edu (the control)
- `epics.compose.extra.now`: EP12 is the epic composer in the poem dropdown.
- `epics.compose.fail`: missed
- `epics.compose.greedy`: greedy
- `epics.compose.mode`: decoding
- `epics.compose.pass`: held
- `epics.compose.pending`: There are no composed verses here yet.
- `epics.compose.sampled`: sampled, temperature 0.8, top 50
- `epics.compose.src`: Lower is better. Every number is read from each run's own training record. Held-out lines: every 20th block of 64 lines of every work, never trained on ({tokens} scored tokens).
- `epics.compose.table.aria`: bits per byte of each run
- `epics.compose.v1`: BASE on the epic lines between 1.75 and 1.95 bpb: measured {m}
- `epics.compose.v2`: EP12 lowers the epic bpb by 0.15 to 0.35 against BASE: measured {m}
- `epics.compose.v3`: FW12 moves the epic bpb by less than 0.03: measured {m}
- `epics.compose.v4`: THE CLAIM: EP12 below FW12 on the epic lines by at least 0.10 bpb: measured {m}
- `epics.compose.v5`: forgetting: EP12's FineWeb TEST rises 0.02 to 0.08 ({a}) and FW12's moves under 0.02 ({b})
- `epics.compose.warn`: An experimental model. It writes lines that sound like an old translation of an epic, and they are often repetitive, ungrammatical or nonsense. It recites nothing. For exact lines, use the epic memories.
- `epics.cueis`: the cue is the {n} characters before line {line}
- `epics.entry`: {chars} characters of text · {mem} of memory · {M} hard locations at {bits} bits a counter
- `epics.error`: could not load the memory: {message}
- `epics.found`: the last {n} characters of your cue are in the poem: the memory reads what was written there
- `epics.line`: start at line
- `epics.load`: LOAD THE MEMORY ({size})
- `epics.loading`: loading: {step}
- `epics.loadingIndex`: looking for epic memories on this server …
- `epics.n`: characters to recite
- `epics.none`: This copy of the site carries no epic memories, so there is nothing to recite here.
- `epics.notfound`: the last {n} characters of your cue are not in the poem: nothing was written at this address, so expect noise
- `epics.notwhole`: not to the end
- `epics.own`: type my own cue
- `epics.ownLabel`: your cue (its last {n} characters are the address)
- `epics.pick`: epic
- `epics.prov`: {title}, {who}, first published {year}. {source}, {licence}.
- `epics.random`: a random line
- `epics.recite`: RECITE
- `epics.short`: your cue has {k} characters; the address reads the last {n}, so a short cue reads an address nobody wrote
- `epics.stat.cps`: characters a second, in this tab
- `epics.stat.nobook`: no book to compare
- `epics.stat.right`: characters right before the first mistake
- `epics.stat.words`: whole words right before the first mistake
- `epics.stop`: STOP
- `epics.text.aria`: the memory reciting {title} from your cue
- `epics.trans`: translated by {tr}
- `epics.verified`: VERIFIED by the builder on this file: reading every position from the true context, {acc}% right; from the first {n} characters, {open} characters right before the first mistake ({whole}); from {cues} random cues, a median of {med} of {span} characters right. Source: {file}.
- `epics.warn`: A memory recites from a cue. It gives back what was written after the last {n} characters of the cue. After its first wrong character it reads its own mistake as context and may wander.

- `film.fs.collapse.title`: The collapse zone: horse, median PSNR (dB) against the pull J
- `film.fs.colour.chart`: Tears of Steel one-shot clip, rb, checkerboard Metropolised Gibbs, TAP J 0.1 (dB)
- `film.fs.colour.plain`: Colour is three grids, one per channel, with no pull between channels. The same rule and read that help the grey horse help the colour clip.
- `film.fs.colour.small`: The first Tears of Steel clip crosses a cut after frame 6, so a new one-shot clip was cut from 40.5 s. It is the player’s fourth clip, with its recorded outputs frame-locked beside it. The cut did not change the median. Checkerboard Metropolised Gibbs with the rb read lifts the colour clip from 35.27 to 40.12 dB at 20 sweeps.
- `film.fs.colour.title`: Colour: a one-shot Tears of Steel clip
- `film.fs.control`: control · {c}
- `film.fs.fit.plain`: TAP computes each lean from a formula. A fit watches what the grid does and corrects the leans until its greys match the target.
- `film.fs.fit.small`: Between J 0.38 and 0.40 the TAP formula stops holding the horse, and the grid flips toward its mirror image. The fitted leans do not collapse up to J 0.44. Where they finally degrade, the chain's slow mixing is the cause, and the leans are fine.
- `film.fs.fit.title`: Leans fitted to the grid, at strong pulls
- `film.fs.inversions`: The inversions against the exact answer on a 4x4 grid (TAP, Bethe, fits, Newton)
- `film.fs.label`: RECORDED · FITTED LEANS
- `film.fs.label.colour`: RECORDED · COLOUR
- `film.fs.label.rb`: RECORDED · THE RB READ
- `film.fs.metro.gibbs`: Gibbs, TAP J 0.2 bits
- `film.fs.metro.title`: bits at J 0.2, TAP leans: Gibbs against Metropolised Gibbs
- `film.fs.mix.bits`: bits 80, J 0.2, TAP, warm (dB) by update rule
- `film.fs.mix.rb`: rb 80, J 0.2 (dB) by update rule
- `film.fs.rb.j01`: J 0.1, TAP leans: dB against sweeps (random-order Gibbs)
- `film.fs.rb.j02`: J 0.2, TAP leans: dB against sweeps (random-order Gibbs)
- `film.fs.rb.plain`: A bit carries two kinds of noise: the coin's own chance, and the motion of its neighbours. The rb read removes the first kind.
- `film.fs.rb.small`: The rb read averages the coin’s probability in place of its result. With no pulls the coin is the only source of noise, so soft and rb both reach 98.75 dB at every budget. With pulls the neighbours’ motion remains. In random order a pixel drawn late in one sweep and early in the next gives two nearly equal values, so rb sits under soft.
- `film.fs.rb.title`: The rb read and the update rules
- `film.fs.tau.small`: 2 tau is how many sweeps one independent sample costs. Metropolised Gibbs makes successive bits anti-correlated (2 tau under 1), which beats the coin law. Near the critical pull (J 0.4, fitted) 2 tau is about 6, and 41% of a bit's variance is the neighbourhood's slow motion, which no read can remove. Swendsen-Wang clusters do not help here, because the picture's leans pin most pixels.
- `film.g1.label`: RECORDED · SWEEPS AND QUALITY
- `film.g1.plain`: A yes-or-no pixel is a coin, and the average of S tosses has a noise floor. More sweeps per frame lower that floor at a fixed rate.
- `film.g1.small`: This is the coin-noise law; g is a pixel's grey in [0, 1]. The Python player is a smooth analogue circuit, so drift limits it instead of noise, and it pulls ahead after about 10 sweeps. From a cold start the p-bits do better, because they forget their starting state in about one sweep.
- `film.g1.title`: More sweeps, a cleaner picture
- `film.g2.label`: RECORDED · LEAN CORRECTIONS
- `film.g2.plain`: Pulls between neighbours smooth the picture but also push every pixel away from its target grey. A lean correction subtracts that push. The better the correction, the stronger the pull the picture survives.
- `film.g2.small`: With no correction the neighbours’ pull lands on top of each pixel’s lean. Mean-field subtracts the pull but over-shoots, and above J = 0.25 the grid flips to its mirror image. TAP adds the Onsager term: part of each neighbour’s pull is this pixel’s own echo. TAP holds the picture to J 0.35.
- `film.g2.title`: Better leans survive stronger pulls
- `film.how.lede.a`: The leans aim each pixel at its grey. The pulls join each pixel to its neighbours. The read averages the answers back into a picture.
- `film.how.lede.b`: The player draws each stage, from the target frame to the error of the read. The recorded numbers come from the Rust runs.
- `film.how.plain`: A grey level can be written as a rate. The player gives each pixel one p-bit; a pixel that should be 70% bright says yes 70% of the time, and the average of its answers recovers the grey.

- `film.rules.checker.cap`: Checkerboard order: the shaded squares first, then the others, the same way every sweep.
- `film.rules.plain`: The rules differ only in how one pixel is redrawn. All of them settle to the same picture. They differ in how much noise their average carries.
- `film.rules.random.cap`: Random order: each sweep visits the pixels in a fresh shuffle.
- `film.rules.small`: Gibbs draws a fresh coin each time. Metropolised Gibbs proposes the other state, so it flips more often and successive bits disagree more; their average is less noisy. On the horse at J 0.2 with TAP leans, bits 80 scores 26.71 dB with Gibbs and 29.68 with checkerboard Metropolised Gibbs. The rb read averages tanh I at the moment each pixel draws instead of the coin’s result, so the coin’s own noise drops out. At J 0.2, rb 80 scores 35.44 dB with random-order Gibbs and 39.88 with checkerboard Metropolised Gibbs. In checkerboard order rb and soft read the same neighbour states, so they almost agree. In random order rb sits 1.25 to 1.6 dB below soft. That is why the player starts on checkerboard Metropolised Gibbs.
- `film.rules.summary`: Update rules and the rb read · default: checkerboard Metropolised Gibbs · now: {now}

The old DJ planned its sets from a hand-written arc. The switch picks which one composes the next set, and a change starts a new set on the next bar line. It is a dev-only switch and resets when the page reloads.

- `gridlearn.lede`: A whole track is a grid of lights: one light a role for each block of 8 bars. A settling machine learned from about eight thousand electronic MIDI arrangements how long layers stay, which roles come in together and where the changes land; these grids are settled from it, and no note of any song is in them. Press play to hear a grid through the house DJ’s own instruments. The hero’s DJ composes its house sets from the same models. Dev builds only.

- `gridlearn.s2.p`: Stage 2 settles a line plan first: where the sections change. A pull puts the kick’s return on a 16- or 32-bar line; the data itself does that about half the time, so the pull is a style choice and its strength was set to reach {target} on house, techno and trance. Inside each block a phrase model settles which bars carry a fill, a roll, a lift, a crash, a drop-out or a bass turnaround, and a groove model settles each bar’s 16 steps from its block’s groove.

These ten pieces were settled and fenced on the Spark; the hero’s DJ deals them into its house sets. A piece is fetched only when you pick it, one at a time.

The chord moves from a cluster to a major chord as the picture forms. When the schedule holds the picture still, the bells ring. MUTE ALL is the one sound choice the site remembers.

- `hero.abstract.boltzmann-curves.label`: Boltzmann curves
- `hero.abstract.boltzmann-curves.note`: the Boltzmann weight e^(-E/T) at four temperatures
- `hero.abstract.branching-tree.label`: a branching tree
- `hero.abstract.branching-tree.note`: a tree grown by splitting each branch in two
- `hero.abstract.bundle-majority.label`: bundling
- `hero.abstract.bundle-majority.note`: seven words and their bundle: each bit is the majority of its column
- `hero.abstract.cell-blanket.label`: a cell's blanket
- `hero.abstract.cell-blanket.note`: a schematic cell: its membrane is a Markov blanket, order inside, scattered disorder outside; the free-energy principle says a living thing stays itself this way
- `hero.abstract.cerebellum-as-sdm.label`: cerebellum as SDM
- `hero.abstract.cerebellum-as-sdm.note`: a schematic of the cerebellum as Kanerva read it: mossy fibres bring the address, granule cells are the hard locations, Purkinje cells sum the votes, a climbing fibre writes
- `hero.abstract.complete-graph.label`: every pair pulled
- `hero.abstract.complete-graph.note`: twelve lights, every pair joined: a fully connected Boltzmann machine
- `hero.abstract.cortex-six-layers.label`: six layers
- `hero.abstract.cortex-six-layers.note`: a schematic of the cortex's six layers: sparse fibres on top, small cells, a dense middle layer, big pyramids reaching the surface; only a few of its cells fire at once, a sparse code
- `hero.abstract.ddyn-arnold-tongues.label`: arnold tongues
- `hero.abstract.ddyn-arnold-tongues.note`: the sine circle map driven at rate Omega (across) with coupling K (up): lit wedges are where drive and oscillator lock to a shared rhythm p/q, all 13 with q up to 6
- `hero.abstract.ddyn-devils-staircase.label`: the devil's staircase
- `hero.abstract.ddyn-devils-staircase.note`: the circle map's winding number against its drive at K = 1: it climbs only in steps, and steps with q up to 13 already cover 0.632 of 4,000 drive values
- `hero.abstract.ddyn-kam-islands.label`: islands of order
- `hero.abstract.ddyn-kam-islands.note`: Chirikov's standard map at K = 1.1: of 126 orbits, the 69 with a near-zero Lyapunov exponent drawn; they ring islands of order inside a chaotic sea
- `hero.abstract.ddyn-onset-measured.label`: the onset, measured
- `hero.abstract.ddyn-onset-measured.note`: Kuramoto oscillators: the steady order r against coupling K for N = 250, 1,000, 4,000, within 0.001 of the Ott-Antonsen law sqrt(1 - Kc / K) above K = 1.4
- `hero.abstract.ddyn-sync-threshold.label`: two chaoses agree
- `hero.abstract.ddyn-sync-threshold.note`: a Lorenz copy pulled toward a Lorenz drive with strength kappa: its conditional Lyapunov exponent falls from 0.91 and crosses zero between 7.75 and 8.0, where the two agree
- `hero.abstract.dendritic-spines.label`: dendritic spines
- `hero.abstract.dendritic-spines.note`: a schematic stretch of dendrite studded with spines, mushroom, thin and stubby; in the cortex most excitatory synapses land on a spine, so a spine holds a weight
- `hero.abstract.dhop-attention-blocks.label`: attention finds its groups
- `hero.abstract.dhop-attention-blocks.note`: 40 tokens attend to one another (softmax, inverse temperature 9); repeated, the update gathers them, and the attention matrix (lit above 1.6/n) turns from a band into 3 blocks of agreement
- `hero.abstract.dhop-capacity-ladder.label`: room grows with order
- `hero.abstract.dhop-capacity-ladder.note`: dense associative memories, energy x^2, x^3, x^4, exp (squares, rings, diamonds, discs): most patterns recalled from 10% noise against units; at 48 units 6, 76, 512, 8,192 or more
- `hero.abstract.dhop-dream-census.label`: dreaming lets go
- `hero.abstract.dhop-dream-census.note`: 40 random starts of a 100-unit Hopfield net with 12 memories: 7 reach a true memory (discs); after 304 dreams of unlearning (Hopfield, Feinstein, Palmer) 28 do, the false ones fade
- `hero.abstract.dhop-one-step-error.label`: one update is enough
- `hero.abstract.dhop-one-step-error.note`: one update of a modern Hopfield net (attention's read) on 12 stored vectors: the error falls as exp(-beta times separation), the line's slope -1.018; rings mark an error of zero in floating point
- `hero.abstract.dhop-phase-diagram.label`: where memory holds
- `hero.abstract.dhop-phase-diagram.note`: where a Hopfield memory holds, load across, temperature up: the line solves the replica equations of Amit, Gutfreund and Sompolinsky; dots are 400-unit runs that kept it (171 of 180 cells agree)
- `hero.abstract.diffusion-aggregate.label`: a diffusion aggregate
- `hero.abstract.diffusion-aggregate.note`: random walkers stick where they touch and grow a branching cluster
- `hero.abstract.dinfo-pentagon-code.label`: shannon's pentagon
- `hero.abstract.dinfo-pentagon-code.note`: five letters, each confusable with its neighbours; five pairs that no reader can mix up (right), and Lovasz's umbrella of five unit vectors (middle) giving Shannon's capacity, the square root of 5
- `hero.abstract.dinfo-perfect-code.label`: a perfect code
- `hero.abstract.dinfo-perfect-code.note`: Hamming(7,4): 16 codewords, each with the 7 words one bit away, tile all 128 words of 7 bits with no overlap, so one flipped bit is always forgiven; its 7 weight-3 words are the Fano plane's lines
- `hero.abstract.dinfo-sdm-bits-ridge.label`: bits a counter returns
- `hero.abstract.dinfo-sdm-bits-ridge.note`: bits each counter of an SDM returns, as patterns are written, for 500, 1,000 and 2,000 hard-locations (thick to thin); a Hopfield net (dots) nears its ceiling of 0.459 bits a weight
- `hero.abstract.dinfo-shannon-limit.label`: a code decoded by settling
- `hero.abstract.dinfo-shannon-limit.note`: a rate 1/2 code read back by p-bits settling at the matched temperature (thick), by belief propagation (dots) and cooled to one state (thin): at flip probability 0.08, 0.0779 wrong becomes 0.0251
- `hero.abstract.dinfo-water-filling.label`: water finds one level
- `hero.abstract.dinfo-water-filling.note`: power 3 poured over 10 parallel noisy channels settles at one level; 6 channels get some, and the capacity is 3.29 bits against 2.732 for an equal share
- `hero.abstract.dlrn-bridge-plane.label`: the bridge on the plane
- `hero.abstract.dlrn-bridge-plane.note`: the loss on the plane through two trained nets (discs) and a bend (ring): the straight path (dashes) crosses a ridge of 0.214, the trained bridge (line) curves round it
- `hero.abstract.dlrn-grok-table.label`: the table made whole
- `hero.abstract.dlrn-grok-table.note`: addition mod 59 as stripes: the net is shown 40% of the table (left) and, after grokking, answers 2,088 of the 2,089 held-out sums right (right)
- `hero.abstract.dlrn-muon-flat.label`: a fair step
- `hero.abstract.dlrn-muon-flat.note`: one weight update's singular values, largest first: gradient descent (left) and Adam (middle) lean on a few directions; Muon's orthogonalised step (right) gives each a fair share, the smallest 0.62
- `hero.abstract.dlrn-room-for-all.label`: room for everyone
- `hero.abstract.dlrn-room-for-all.note`: five features in two dimensions at sparsity 0, 0.5, 0.8 and 0.95: as features grow rarer the net makes room for 2, 3, then all 5
- `hero.abstract.dlrn-sdm-grad-rows.label`: where the gradient goes
- `hero.abstract.dlrn-sdm-grad-rows.note`: our SDM model's gradient on one batch, rows sorted by size, a log scale: the largest 10% of the rows it reaches hold 92.2% to 99.5% of the squared gradient, in each of four hops
- `hero.abstract.double-well-contours.label`: a double well
- `hero.abstract.double-well-contours.note`: the contours of a double-well energy: two valleys and the ridge between them
- `hero.abstract.dqua-anneal-time.label`: three gentle roads
- `hero.abstract.dqua-anneal-time.note`: one SETTLE puzzle annealed three ways (quantum, p-bit replicas, Gibbs), success against effort: quantum annealing rises from 0.014 to 0.999; the axes are not one currency
- `hero.abstract.dqua-bell-polytope.label`: more than any script
- `hero.abstract.dqua-bell-polytope.note`: two correlations of a shared pair: every local script stays in the diamond, a singlet measured at random angles reaches the circle; sampled, S = 2.82 against Bell's local 2.01
- `hero.abstract.dqua-qaoa-landscape.label`: a fair split
- `hero.abstract.dqua-qaoa-landscape.note`: QAOA's one-layer energy over its two angles (the optimum ringed) beside the puzzle it solves: 10 spins, a SETTLE max-cut, split so 13 of 15 pulls are kept apart
- `hero.abstract.dqua-rabi-chevron.label`: the swing, mapped
- `hero.abstract.dqua-rabi-chevron.note`: a qubit driven at its own frequency swings fully from 0 to 1; detuned by the drive's strength the swing is 0.5, by three times it 0.1: the Rabi chevron as contour lines
- `hero.abstract.dqua-threshold-cross.label`: the threshold crossing
- `hero.abstract.dqua-threshold-cross.note`: repetition codes of 1 to 9 qubits, a majority read like an SDM's: at a 0.1 flip probability the error falls from 0.1 to 0.00089; all curves meet at one half
- `hero.abstract.dragon-curve.label`: a dragon curve
- `hero.abstract.dragon-curve.note`: a strip of paper folded in half twelve times and opened at right angles
- `hero.abstract.dropout-network.label`: dropout
- `hero.abstract.dropout-network.note`: a network with some hidden units dropped for one step
- `hero.abstract.dscale-capacity-line.label`: room grows with the store
- `hero.abstract.dscale-capacity-line.note`: a Kanerva SDM's capacity as its hard-locations grow from 500 to 16,000: waking 1% of them, it rises with slope 1.0; waking 32, with slope 0.82
- `hero.abstract.dscale-data-repeats.label`: the text comes round again
- `hero.abstract.dscale-data-repeats.note`: our best SDM recipe learning over 200M tokens drawn from a 65,522,263-token shard; at each dashed line the text it reads starts to repeat
- `hero.abstract.dscale-grid-measured.label`: the wide keep learning
- `hero.abstract.dscale-grid-measured.note`: our SDM model (discs) and a transformer (squares) on fresh text, 6 widths, 100M to 1.6B tokens: from 400M to 1.6B the width 256 SDM gains 0.001 bits, width 768 gains 0.013
- `hero.abstract.dscale-windows-agree.label`: two seeds, one opinion
- `hero.abstract.dscale-windows-agree.note`: 3,892 test windows scored by our model trained twice from different random starts: each dot is one window, and the two runs agree on which text is hard, r = 0.9977
- `hero.abstract.dsdm-critical-collapse.label`: one curve
- `hero.abstract.dsdm-critical-collapse.note`: a real SDM's critical-distance for 4 store sizes: apart against words per hard-location, together once the shared-location noise is counted (spread 23.2 to 11.4 bits)
- `hero.abstract.dsdm-lens-exponential.label`: the lens is an exponential
- `hero.abstract.dsdm-lens-exponential.note`: two activation circles in 1,000 bits share a lens that shrinks as an exponential of their Hamming distance (beta 5.59, R squared 0.997): an SDM read is softmax attention near home
- `hero.abstract.dsdm-mixer-shares.label`: neighbours share
- `hero.abstract.dsdm-mixer-shares.note`: our SDM mixer's product-key addresses, each partner at its true angle: the closer, the more locations shared (beta 4.05, R squared 0.994); Kanerva's lens, the rings, gives 4.27
- `hero.abstract.dsdm-radius-temperature.label`: the radius is a temperature
- `hero.abstract.dsdm-radius-temperature.note`: an SDM's activation-radius is attention's temperature: beta against the share of space a circle holds, for 64, 256 and 1,000 bits (3.96, 4.19, 4.16 at 1%); our mixer, the star, 4.05
- `hero.abstract.dsdm-two-homes-flow.label`: two homes
- `hero.abstract.dsdm-two-homes-flow.note`: a real SDM holding 20 words: each arrow is where one read carries an address in the plane of two words 128 bits apart; both welcome their neighbours home, noise rests between
- `hero.abstract.dspr-columns-curve.label`: more columns, fewer touches
- `hero.abstract.dspr-columns-curve.note`: sensations to recognise one object among 1,000, over 1,000 trials: 7.28 for one column, 2.92 for four that vote, 1.43 for ten; six that do not vote need 8.66
- `hero.abstract.dspr-false-match-cliff.label`: the false-match cliff
- `hero.abstract.dspr-false-match-cliff.note`: two random 40-bit codes in 2,048 bits share 0.78 bits on average; the probability they share 20 is 2.5e-26, and in 200,000 draws none shared more than 7
- `hero.abstract.dspr-fields-learned.label`: sixty-four fields
- `hero.abstract.dspr-fields-learned.note`: the 64 fields a boosted spatial pooler learned from random bar patterns: 53 are one clean row or column, and each of the 16 bars is held by 4 to 6 columns
- `hero.abstract.dspr-neighbours-share.label`: neighbours share
- `hero.abstract.dspr-neighbours-share.note`: a random distributed scalar encoder: the value 0 shares 30 of its 40 bits with the value 10, 20 with 20, and at most 1 from 40 apart, so near values overlap
- `hero.abstract.dspr-ours-overlap.label`: shared meeting places
- `hero.abstract.dspr-ours-overlap.note`: locations two tokens' reads share in our SDM model, of 32: 0.016 by chance, 4.1 for random pairs, 5.6 for the same next token, 6.7 for neighbours, 11.4 for the same token
- `hero.abstract.dthm-coalescence-time.label`: the time to agree
- `hero.abstract.dthm-coalescence-time.note`: two chains, all up and all down, fed the same random numbers: the median sweeps until they agree rises from 15 at T 4 to 1,810 at T 2.3 on a 32 x 32 lattice, and below the critical temperature they wait
- `hero.abstract.dthm-healing-contours.label`: healing rings
- `hero.abstract.dthm-healing-contours.note`: an island of minus spins, radius 40, in a sea of plus at T 1: its outline every 200 sweeps, nested, closing in; its area falls 3.631 a sweep in a straight line and is gone by sweep 1,250
- `hero.abstract.dthm-kramers-wannier.label`: hot and cold meet
- `hero.abstract.dthm-kramers-wannier.note`: Kramers-Wannier duality, sinh 2K sinh 2K* = 1: the hot Ising model at K 0.25 and the cold one at K* 0.7034 are one model seen twice; hot and cold meet at K = 0.4407, the critical point
- `hero.abstract.dthm-kz-slope.label`: fewer walls, slower
- `hero.abstract.dthm-kz-slope.note`: the walls a cooling leaves behind, measured on a 256 x 256 Ising lattice over 8 runs: slower cooling, fewer walls, from 7.95% to 0.91% of bonds broken, slope -0.455 in log-log
- `hero.abstract.dthm-two-solids-peak.label`: the fair share
- `hero.abstract.dthm-two-solids-peak.note`: two Einstein solids, one twice the other, share their energy: the number of ways peaks near a third, the fair share, and grows 3.94 times narrower as the solids grow 16 times
- `hero.abstract.dvsa-algebras-curves.label`: four algebras hold pairs
- `hero.abstract.dvsa-algebras-curves.note`: pairs bound and bundled in 512 numbers, each read back among 100 fillers: at 40 pairs FHRR reads 99%, MAP reads 83%, HRR reads 82%, binary 61%; MAP sits on its theory line
- `hero.abstract.dvsa-block-code-grid.label`: a block code binds
- `hero.abstract.dvsa-block-code-grid.note`: a sparse block code vector, 12 blocks of 8 cells with one lit in each: binding adds the two lit positions in every block, and subtracting gives b back exactly
- `hero.abstract.dvsa-capacity-arms.label`: four ways to resonate
- `hero.abstract.dvsa-capacity-arms.note`: a resonator untangling hypervectors bound from three factors, 256 bits wide: by sign it settles 90% to 32 rows a codebook; a threshold and a little noise carry it to 64
- `hero.abstract.dvsa-kernel-family.label`: spread and kernel
- `hero.abstract.dvsa-kernel-family.note`: a phasor vector's phases spread wide, clustered or heavy-tailed (rings) make a sinc, a Gaussian and a Laplace similarity kernel; 2,048 phasors land within 0.04 of the theory
- `hero.abstract.dvsa-peel-gain.label`: everyone gets heard
- `hero.abstract.dvsa-peel-gain.note`: a sum of K random vectors read back among 1,000: the plain top-K finds 72% of 80 members, peeling the loudest away one by one finds 99%
- `hero.abstract.eaip-basin-circles.label`: room for every memory
- `hero.abstract.eaip-basin-circles.note`: each stored pattern's basin as a circle (the most flipped bits it still recalls from): one stored 3 times as strongly holds 54, the rest 12 to 24; all equal, 36 to 42
- `hero.abstract.eaip-cue-completion.label`: a part calls the whole
- `hero.abstract.eaip-cue-completion.note`: a Hopfield network of 300 units recalls a pattern from a part of it: at loads of 15, 30 and 42 patterns, half the recalls succeed once 0.2, 0.4 and 0.55 of it is given
- `hero.abstract.eaip-energy-two-censuses.label`: where the starts settle
- `hero.abstract.eaip-energy-two-censuses.note`: the energies 500 random starts settle to in a Hopfield model, each rung as long as its share: one pattern stored strongly takes 94% (left); equal, 14% (right)
- `hero.abstract.eaip-free-energy-cross.label`: where the basins trade
- `hero.abstract.eaip-free-energy-cross.note`: a model: the wide basin's free energy minus the narrow well's, -T ln Z for each, against temperature: below 0.071 the deep well wins, above it the wide basin, by its room
- `hero.abstract.eaip-memory-constellation.label`: a memory linked in
- `hero.abstract.eaip-memory-constellation.note`: 13 stored patterns of a memory in three families, linked where their overlap passes 0.3; a newcomer made of two families (ringed) joins both, by 6 links
- `hero.abstract.econd-basin-shares.label`: two memories share
- `hero.abstract.econd-basin-shares.note`: a Hopfield net holds two memories: the share of 240 random starts that settle to the second grows from 0.22 to 0.79 as its strength goes from half to twice the first's, 0.55 at equal
- `hero.abstract.econd-domain-area-law.label`: domains close evenly
- `hero.abstract.econd-domain-area-law.note`: minus discs of radius 6, 9 and 12 in a plus Ising lattice at T 1.5 close along nearly straight lines, losing about 3.47, 5.02 and 5.24 sites a sweep until each is gone
- `hero.abstract.econd-forest-of-chains.label`: many short chains
- `hero.abstract.econd-forest-of-chains.note`: 16 short Gibbs chains of 40 sweeps each estimate an Ising energy: 10 of their naive intervals miss the long chain's -1.054 (dotted); the pooled diamond lands at -1.06
- `hero.abstract.econd-ladder-braid.label`: a braid of walkers
- `hero.abstract.econd-ladder-braid.note`: four walkers on one rugged line swap temperatures: their paths through T 0.12, 0.3, 0.7 and 1.6 over 36 rounds braid together, 5 round trips from coldest to hottest and back
- `hero.abstract.econd-relaxation-vs-size.label`: bigger takes longer
- `hero.abstract.econd-relaxation-vs-size.note`: heat-bath Ising lattices of side 4 to 24 cooled to T 1.6 from noise: the median sweeps to 90% order rise from 2 to 65.5, a slope near 1.94 on log axes
- `hero.abstract.edeb-common-ground.label`: common ground
- `hero.abstract.edeb-common-ground.note`: two rings of 9 p-bits start in opposite states; with 3 bridges, Gibbs cooling brings every one to agree in 40 of 40 runs; with no bridges, in 1
- `hero.abstract.edeb-funnel.label`: many samplers, one answer
- `hero.abstract.edeb-funnel.note`: 60 Metropolis samplers of one 12-spin ring, 21 to 1,195 sweeps long: short ones scatter, long ones gather, and their weighted pool reads 0.393 against the exact 0.379
- `hero.abstract.edeb-overlap.label`: two nudges, shared ground
- `hero.abstract.edeb-overlap.note`: a ring's exact magnetisation under no field and under two small fields: effect sizes d = 0.41 and 0.74, yet the two distributions share 83% and 71% of their probability
- `hero.abstract.edeb-power-curve.label`: how many samples see it
- `hero.abstract.edeb-power-curve.note`: the probability a two-sample test sees each nudge, against samples per arm: 80% needs about 95 draws for the small one and 29 for the large one, 3.2 times fewer
- `hero.abstract.edeb-pruned-recall.label`: the picture stays whole
- `hero.abstract.edeb-pruned-recall.note`: a Hopfield memory of 384 units holding four calm shapes recalls its ring from a cue 18% wrong with 0, 60, 90 and 97% of its weights removed: overlaps 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.92
- `hero.abstract.eevid-certainty-cools.label`: certainty as cooling
- `hero.abstract.eevid-certainty-cools.note`: all 65,536 states of a 4 x 4 Ising magnet, weighed exactly: as T falls from 5.0 to 1.6 the chance of all spins agreeing grows from 0.9% to 87.8%
- `hero.abstract.eevid-detailed-balance.label`: detailed balance
- `hero.abstract.eevid-detailed-balance.note`: a model: a three-state Metropolis chain at T 1 settles to Boltzmann's weights 0.524, 0.318 and 0.158; every flow one way is matched by its flow back
- `hero.abstract.eevid-effect-gap.label`: the gap between two
- `hero.abstract.eevid-effect-gap.note`: a model: a 16 x 16 Ising lattice sampled at T 3.2 (filled) and 2.4 (outline), 400 samples each: mean energy per site -0.747 and -1.239, a gap of d = 3.39
- `hero.abstract.eevid-eight-step.label`: eight steps of cooling
- `hero.abstract.eevid-eight-step.note`: a metaphor: eight cooling steps on a 0 to 10 scale take a 28 x 28 Ising lattice from -0.48 to -2.00 energy per site; a scan finds 0 stray high-energy sites
- `hero.abstract.eevid-funnel.label`: a funnel of small runs
- `hero.abstract.eevid-funnel.note`: a model: 160 small runs of one p-bit, 4 to 396 samples each, estimate its lean of 0.4; small runs scatter wide and 95.6% fall inside the 95% funnel
- `hero.abstract.ehist-anneal-beats-quench.label`: anneal, not quench
- `hero.abstract.ehist-anneal-beats-quench.note`: a rugged Ising landscape with random fields, averaged over 8 lattices: frozen at once (line) it stops at energy -1.77, cooled slowly (dashes) it finds -1.94
- `hero.abstract.ehist-order-arrives.label`: agreement arrives
- `hero.abstract.ehist-order-arrives.note`: Kuramoto oscillators with spread natural rhythms: below K_c = 1 no common beat, above it one grows; at K = 3 measured 0.81 (rings), Kuramoto's exact curve 0.82
- `hero.abstract.ehist-tree-of-help.label`: a tree of help
- `hero.abstract.ehist-tree-of-help.note`: bond percolation at p = 0.6 on a 40 x 22 lattice: the tree by which help reaches 805 sites from one, breadth first, across the whole width
- `hero.abstract.ehist-two-memories-share.label`: two memories, one base
- `hero.abstract.ehist-two-memories-share.note`: two pictures stored in one Hopfield network share 511 of their 24 x 24 bits: energy along the path between them has two valleys and a ridge 7.3 high
- `hero.abstract.ehist-well-and-basin.label`: from a narrow well
- `hero.abstract.ehist-well-and-basin.note`: a picture of a metaphor, not a mechanism: a narrow well and a wide lower basin; at T 0.1 the Boltzmann weight puts 98% in the basin, at T 0.5 77%
- `hero.abstract.emech-basin-moves.label`: the basin moves
- `hero.abstract.emech-basin-moves.note`: a Hopfield memory of a broken ring: filling its 42-cell gap climbs the energy (dashed); after the whole ring is written back the same walk runs downhill (solid)
- `hero.abstract.emech-escape-rates.label`: over the barrier
- `hero.abstract.emech-escape-rates.note`: Metropolis walkers timed over the double well B(x^2 - 1)^2 at T 0.3 for six barriers: log(rate / B) falls in a straight line of slope -0.98, the Arrhenius law
- `hero.abstract.emech-lock-in.label`: locking in
- `hero.abstract.emech-lock-in.note`: two Kuramoto groups of oscillators, each in step inside, beating at 1.0 and 1.5: as the bond between them grows their phases lock, past 0.9 from a bond of 0.25
- `hero.abstract.emech-quench-vs-anneal.label`: cold, then slowly
- `hero.abstract.emech-quench-vs-anneal.note`: 400 walkers on a rugged energy landscape, 3,600 Metropolis steps each: held cold, 18% find the deepest valley; cooled slowly, 80% do
- `hero.abstract.emech-room-curve.label`: room while busy
- `hero.abstract.emech-room-curve.note`: a Hopfield net of 400 units holding 20 patterns recalls one while some units are busy: it keeps overlap 0.577 with 200 busy and falls under one half only at 240
- `hero.abstract.energy-landscape.label`: energy landscape
- `hero.abstract.energy-landscape.note`: a rugged energy curve and a ball resting in its deepest valley
- `hero.abstract.eprac-eight-stops.label`: eight stops of a cooling
- `hero.abstract.eprac-eight-stops.note`: all 65,536 states of a 4 x 4 Ising lattice give Z(T) exactly: energy, free energy (bold) and TS per spin; eight stops of a cooling schedule, free energy -3.05 at T 4 falling to -2.044 at T 1
- `hero.abstract.eprac-found-from-fragment.label`: found from a fragment
- `hero.abstract.eprac-found-from-fragment.note`: a real SDM of 3,000 hard-locations in 256 bits holds 16 words; a fragment 64 bits from one word is read again and again: Hamming distance 24, 0, 0, 0
- `hero.abstract.eprac-ladder-temperature.label`: rungs at five temperatures
- `hero.abstract.eprac-ladder-temperature.note`: eleven energy rungs, 0 to 10, and their Boltzmann occupation at five temperatures from 8 down to 0.5: the mean rung falls from 3.79 to 0.16; a 0 to 10 scale drawn as a temperature, a metaphor only
- `hero.abstract.eprac-own-memory.label`: its own memory
- `hero.abstract.eprac-own-memory.note`: a Hopfield memory of 160 units holds 4 shapes; a cue with 40 units turned settles, unled, to its own ring (overlap 1); a gentle field of 0.35 toward another shape leads it away (small)
- `hero.abstract.eprac-soft-threshold.label`: a soft threshold
- `hero.abstract.eprac-soft-threshold.note`: a p-bit outputs sgn(tanh(beta I) - r) with r uniform: the curves are tanh(beta I) at four betas, the squares the means of 400 samples, never more than 0.102 from the curve
- `hero.abstract.eprot-critical-slowing.label`: slow near the edge
- `hero.abstract.eprot-critical-slowing.note`: a 24 x 24 lattice under Gibbs sweeps: the sweeps it needs to forget its magnetisation peak near T 2.3 (dashed: Onsager's 2.27), 72 there against 1 cold and 2 hot
- `hero.abstract.eprot-escape-times.label`: leaving a well
- `hero.abstract.eprot-escape-times.note`: 300 Metropolis walkers timed leaving a well: the mean time grows 29-fold as barrier over temperature goes 2 to 7, a log slope of 0.7 (Arrhenius: 1 for high walls)
- `hero.abstract.eprot-free-energy.label`: free energy, exactly
- `hero.abstract.eprot-free-energy.note`: a 4 x 4 lattice summed over all 65,536 states: free energy per spin (thick) falls from -2.026 to -3.679 as it warms, entropy (dashed) climbs to 0.644, near ln 2 = 0.693
- `hero.abstract.eprot-gentlest-compromise.label`: one unhappy bond each
- `hero.abstract.eprot-gentlest-compromise.note`: spins that prefer to differ, on a triangular lattice: no triangle can please all three bonds; cooled, 162 of its 162 triangles keep exactly one unhappy bond (dashed), the gentlest share
- `hero.abstract.eprot-schedule-shapes.label`: four ways to cool
- `hero.abstract.eprot-schedule-shapes.note`: four ways to cool a 32 x 32 lattice in 240 sweeps, 24 runs each; bars show the bonds left unsettled: quench 0.9%, linear 0.8%, exponential 0.8%, stairs 1.1%
- `hero.abstract.esci-arrhenius-line.label`: time to cross a barrier
- `hero.abstract.esci-arrhenius-line.note`: Metropolis walkers at T 0.25 timed to cross a barrier B from 0.2 to 1.0: ln of the mean time is a straight line in B, slope 2.57 (1/T is 4), the crossing 7.7 times slower at the top
- `hero.abstract.esci-eleven-temperatures.label`: eleven temperatures
- `hero.abstract.esci-eleven-temperatures.note`: energy per spin of a 32 x 32 Ising lattice at eleven temperatures, 0 to 10 on the axis, from -2.00 to -0.67, steepest from T 2.25 to 2.5 (a 0 to 10 scale drawn as temperature, a metaphor)
- `hero.abstract.esci-two-memories-share.label`: two memories share a bridge
- `hero.abstract.esci-two-memories-share.note`: a hopfield network of 384 units holds two pictures that share a bridge; each cued from its own outer third comes back whole, bridge included: every one of its 384 units right
- `hero.abstract.esci-two-wells-free-energy.label`: breadth counts too
- `hero.abstract.esci-two-wells-free-energy.note`: the free energy F = -T ln Z of a narrow well and a wide basin on one landscape: the wide one is lower at every temperature, by 0.15 near T 0 and 0.54 at T 0.4, as its breadth adds entropy
- `hero.abstract.esci-update-and-strength.label`: strong words change slowly
- `hero.abstract.esci-update-and-strength.note`: a Kanerva SDM word written 1, 2, 4 or 8 times, then a new word written at its address: the read turns to the new word after 2, 3, 5 and 9 writes, one more than its count each time (a model)
- `hero.abstract.evar-butterfly-settled.label`: one wing remembers the other
- `hero.abstract.evar-butterfly-settled.note`: a butterfly stored as one hopfield memory; given the left wing, gibbs sweeps fill in the right: its 1,240 cells go from overlap 0.01 to 1.00
- `hero.abstract.evar-detailed-balance.label`: every give, a take
- `hero.abstract.evar-detailed-balance.note`: four states on a ring, metropolis moves between neighbours at temperature 1: each flow one way equals the flow back (0.109, 0.060, 0.060, 0.133), detailed balance
- `hero.abstract.evar-eight-step-schedule.label`: eight steps of cooling
- `hero.abstract.evar-eight-step-schedule.note`: a cooling schedule of eight steps, T 3.0 to 0.3, on a 32 by 32 ising lattice: energy per spin falls from -0.64 to -1.87. eight steps like the eight phases of emdr, a picture only
- `hero.abstract.evar-free-energy.label`: free energy, summed exactly
- `hero.abstract.evar-free-energy.note`: all 65,536 states of a 4 by 4 ising lattice summed exactly: energy, free energy and the dotted T S, with the heat capacity's peak at T 2.45 where order arrives
- `hero.abstract.evar-two-basins.label`: a narrow well, a wide basin
- `hero.abstract.evar-two-basins.note`: a deep narrow well and a wide calm basin whose floor is 1.26 higher: at temperature 1 the wide one holds 0.71 of the boltzmann probability; at 0.5 the narrow one holds 0.53
- `hero.abstract.fhops-fork.label`: the fork
- `hero.abstract.fhops-fork.note`: two sequences of 8 words share word 4: an SDM read addressed by the last word leaves the fork 64 and 60 bits from the two roads and ends on the wrong one; by the last two words, 0 bits wrong
- `hero.abstract.fhops-four-hop-arcs.label`: four hops
- `hero.abstract.fhops-four-hop-arcs.note`: our trained SDM model on real text: 14 contexts, each read becoming the next address four times; each hop's read moves the working vector 3.8 to 4.8 against its length 105
- `hero.abstract.fhops-graded-reach.label`: two read rules
- `hero.abstract.fhops-graded-reach.note`: one SDM read two ways, 120 noisy reads at each start: every woken hard-location votes 1, or votes by how far inside the activation-radius it lies; from 64 bits off 68 against 70 come home
- `hero.abstract.fhops-slow-at-the-edge.label`: slow at the edge
- `hero.abstract.fhops-slow-at-the-edge.note`: a small SDM holding 40 words, read again and again from noisy copies: a square is the share home by that hop; from 16 bits off 20 of 40 arrive in one hop, from 64 bits 15 arrive, the last at hop 9
- `hero.abstract.fhops-two-weights.label`: two weights
- `hero.abstract.fhops-two-weights.note`: one real read of our trained model, its 64 candidate scores weighted two ways: the soft cut-off gives every one 0.16 to 0.5, 25% of it below the 32nd; the graded rule spreads it over 25.9 locations
- `hero.abstract.fhrr-bag-vs-order.label`: a bag and an order
- `hero.abstract.fhrr-bag-vs-order.note`: dog bites man and man bites dog as a plain bundle are the same vector (cosine 1.0); with each word shifted by its place the cosine falls to 0.31
- `hero.abstract.fhrr-capacity-line.label`: a trace holds pairs
- `hero.abstract.fhrr-capacity-line.note`: pairs one trace holds with 100 possible fillers and 99% of reads right, measured for six widths n: about one pair per 26.6 numbers, a straight line
- `hero.abstract.fhrr-involution.label`: the involution
- `hero.abstract.fhrr-involution.note`: a vector, the same read backwards (its involution), and their circular convolution: a spike of 1.11 at zero over noise of about 0.103, so unbinding returns a noisy copy
- `hero.abstract.fhrr-place-in-plane.label`: three places in one vector
- `hero.abstract.fhrr-place-in-plane.note`: three points of a plane, each the fractional powers X^x and Y^y bound together, bundled into one 2,048-number vector; its similarity over the plane rises to about 1 at each point (0.98, 0.98, 0.97)
- `hero.abstract.fhrr-wrapped-diagonals.label`: the wrapped diagonals
- `hero.abstract.fhrr-wrapped-diagonals.note`: Plate's bind, circular convolution: the outer product of two 12-number vectors (the square) summed down each wrapped diagonal gives one entry of the bound vector (right)
- `hero.abstract.fkeys-collision.label`: two contexts, one address
- `hero.abstract.fkeys-collision.note`: locations shared by two positions of real text, over 8,386,560 pairs in our trained model, log scale: 79.08% share none, 14.62% all 32; 4,096 positions wake 2,036 of 65,536
- `hero.abstract.fkeys-cost.label`: the price of an address
- `hero.abstract.fkeys-cost.note`: product keys score 2 x 256 = 512 half sub-keys instead of all 65,536 locations of the SDM, 256 times fewer multiply-adds, then sum a 64 x 64 block, and still find the same best cells
- `hero.abstract.fkeys-hash-bins.label`: a hash address is shared
- `hero.abstract.fkeys-hash-bins.note`: the exact bigram address of our n-gram table: 3,901,614 distinct bigrams in 20 million tokens of our text on 65,536 rows, 59.5 a row, spread 7.541 against Poisson's 7.716
- `hero.abstract.fkeys-staircase.label`: the best cells form a staircase
- `hero.abstract.fkeys-staircase.note`: rows and columns sorted by half score: the best 32 locations fill a staircase in the corner at all 4,096 positions, so the best 64 of each half hold them; at the start 13 by 8, trained 10 by 4
- `hero.abstract.fkeys-two-rows.label`: two rows choose the cells
- `hero.abstract.fkeys-two-rows.note`: our trained model at one position of real text: the best half-one sub-key scores along the top, the best half-two down the side; its 32 woken locations sit where they cross, 10 columns by 4 rows
- `hero.abstract.floop-age-curve.label`: a store ages
- `hero.abstract.floop-age-curve.note`: read-back against a fact's age after 1,000 writes in 1,024 numbers: a plain sum (dashed) reads 20% at any age; fading by 0.99 or 0.97 keeps the newest and drops below half by age 75 or 55
- `hero.abstract.floop-capacity-fidelity.label`: how far it unfolds
- `hero.abstract.floop-capacity-fidelity.note`: how far a phrase unfolds right before its first wrong letter, against the facts in one vector of 256, 1,024 and 4,096 numbers: half way by 37, 109 and 525 facts
- `hero.abstract.floop-sequence-chain.label`: the walk loops
- `hero.abstract.floop-sequence-chain.note`: generation as a walk on a store's 26 two-letter contexts (thin lines are its 30 facts): from 'an' (ringed) it runs 3 steps, then loops on a cycle of 10 forever
- `hero.abstract.floop-the-cycle.label`: enfold, unfold
- `hero.abstract.floop-the-cycle.note`: one cycle of a real store: the address 'the' (left) unbinds a vector of 1,024 counters holding 13 facts (top); the noisy read (60% right) cleans up to N
- `hero.abstract.floop-window-roll.label`: the window rolls
- `hero.abstract.floop-window-roll.note`: our SDM model's address over time: a token steps through the 8 back slots, then lives on only in 5 running averages; 15 steps on, the 0.99 average keeps 86% of it
- `hero.abstract.fourier-square.label`: Fourier sums
- `hero.abstract.fourier-square.note`: a square wave built from one, three, nine and 25 sine waves
- `hero.abstract.fours-four-tables.label`: four tables
- `hero.abstract.fours-four-tables.note`: one real context wakes 32 of 65,536 locations in each of its four hop tables: in hops 1 and 2 they fill 3 columns, in hops 3 and 4 one row of the 256 x 256 grid
- `hero.abstract.fours-one-location.label`: one busy location
- `hero.abstract.fours-one-location.note`: the hop-1 location our model woke most while reading 2,560 tokens, 766 times; its value row against the token table pushes a comma, a full stop and 'and'
- `hero.abstract.fours-path-barcodes.label`: the read path
- `hero.abstract.fours-path-barcodes.note`: one real read as the sign bits of its vectors: 13 features, the working vector, then each of 4 hops flipping 6, 2, 3 and 5 of 256 bits, then the token 'time'
- `hero.abstract.fours-soft-cutoff.label`: a soft cut-off
- `hero.abstract.fours-soft-cutoff.note`: one real read's 64 candidate locations, weight sigmoid((s - theta) / 0.25): 0.74 to 0.28 at hop 1, all within 0.49 to 0.50 at hop 4, so the cut-off barely cuts
- `hero.abstract.fours-thirteen-features.label`: the address
- `hero.abstract.fours-thirteen-features.note`: our trained model's address is 8 back tokens and 5 running averages; each bar is how much its input map takes from one: the last token 40.2, the token 7 back 3.7
- `hero.abstract.fread-cleanup-crossing.label`: where cleanup fails
- `hero.abstract.fread-cleanup-crossing.note`: unbinding one fact from bundles of 1 to 512 in 1,024 dimensions: its cos falls as 1/sqrt(K) (line, dots) to the best of 999 wrong vectors (dashed, 0.1017); they cross near K = 96.6
- `hero.abstract.fread-complicate-strips.label`: complicate to explicate
- `hero.abstract.fread-complicate-strips.note`: the Complicate of 3 bound facts in 128 coordinates, unbound by one address, then cleaned against 26 codebook rows: the Explicate is the stored value exactly, 32 coordinates corrected (ticks)
- `hero.abstract.fread-query-among-stars.label`: a read among the stars
- `hero.abstract.fread-query-among-stars.note`: one fact unbound from a bundle of 4 in 1,024 dimensions: 600 codebook vectors placed by 1 - cos to the read; the wrong ones crowd a ring (cos at most 0.096), the right one sits inside at 0.505
- `hero.abstract.fread-ranked-similarities.label`: one step above the noise
- `hero.abstract.fread-ranked-similarities.note`: an unbound read against 64 codebook vectors, sorted: the stored one at cos 0.377 (1/sqrt(8) is 0.354), the next at 0.067, 62 of 63 inside the noise band 2/sqrt(D)
- `hero.abstract.fread-read-funnel.label`: the read funnel
- `hero.abstract.fread-read-funnel.note`: iterated-reads of a real SDM (1,500 hard-locations, 50 words of 256 bits): every read from 30 bits off or nearer pours into the stored word; from 48 bits on, none does
- `hero.abstract.frun-copy-arcs.label`: copy arcs
- `hero.abstract.frun-copy-arcs.note`: a real 256-token window: 28 positions share 4 or more of 8 woken SDM locations with an earlier one, each arcing back to the token that one wrote; in 4 (bold) it is the token that comes next
- `hero.abstract.frun-past-eight.label`: past the eight
- `hero.abstract.frun-past-eight.note`: how far back the run-time write's strongest read reaches, for 1,510 reads sharing 4 or more of 8 SDM locations: 83.6% reach past the 8 back tokens, the median 30 back
- `hero.abstract.frun-shared-context.label`: shared context
- `hero.abstract.frun-shared-context.note`: 48 real windows: positions sharing none of their 8 back tokens share 0.03 of 8 woken SDM locations, one shared token 1.22, all 8 6.23: the address follows the context
- `hero.abstract.frun-shuffle-control.label`: the shuffled control
- `hero.abstract.frun-shuffle-control.note`: the raw run-time read, cleaned up against the token table, names the next token first at 909 of 5,014 positions in 48 windows where it occurred earlier; with the SDM writes shuffled, 173
- `hero.abstract.frun-who-reads-whom.label`: who reads whom
- `hero.abstract.frun-who-reads-whom.note`: a real window through our run-time write: each star is the earlier position whose SDM locations a later one reads most; circled, 4 of 7 tokens of a phrase read its copy 112 tokens back
- `hero.abstract.fsdm-between-two-words.label`: between two words
- `hero.abstract.fsdm-between-two-words.note`: read-addresses stepping from a stored A to a stored H, 457 bits apart, each read iterated in a real SDM: the first 4 come back A, the last 3 H; the switch is a clean step between two neighbours, the edge of the two basins
- `hero.abstract.fsdm-cobweb-reads.label`: a cobweb of reads
- `hero.abstract.fsdm-cobweb-reads.note`: the mean distance after one read of a real SDM (6,000 hard-locations, 100 words of 1,000 bits), iterated as a cobweb: from 190 bits off it steps down to the word; past the critical-distance 236 a read lands farther than it began
- `hero.abstract.fsdm-noise-for-strangers.label`: noise for strangers
- `hero.abstract.fsdm-noise-for-strangers.note`: a real SDM holding 60 words, 3 of them letters: copies of A and S with 150 of 1,000 bits flipped read back whole; a never-stored address reads back noise, 325 bits from every word
- `hero.abstract.fsdm-two-distances.label`: two distances
- `hero.abstract.fsdm-two-distances.note`: 20,000 hard-locations placed by Hamming distance from a write-address and a read-address 100 bits apart: 127 lie within 460 of the first, 112 of the second, 34 of both
- `hero.abstract.fsdm-two-ways-to-wake.label`: two ways to wake
- `hero.abstract.fsdm-two-ways-to-wake.note`: a real SDM's hard-locations by address distance from a noisy A (across) and counter agreement (up): the address read wakes 128 of them, the KANERVA crate's content read wakes 135
- `hero.abstract.ftrain-four-machines.label`: one run, four machines
- `hero.abstract.ftrain-four-machines.note`: the same SDM training run, same seed and tokens, on four GPUs: TEST bits per byte from 1.663 to 1.670, a spread of 0.007, the noise any smaller difference sits in
- `hero.abstract.ftrain-reads-measured.label`: what the reads add
- `hero.abstract.ftrain-reads-measured.note`: measured at 20M tokens: no memory reads 1.662 bits per byte, trained SDM reads 1.668, a small dense layer 1.586; zero the reads after training: 2.672
- `hero.abstract.ftrain-tokenizers.label`: tokenizers at equal bytes
- `hero.abstract.ftrain-tokenizers.note`: four tokenizers for our SDM model on the same 95.4M bytes, square area its vocabulary: bits per byte 1.638, 1.637, 1.653 and 1.658, from 16k to 129k
- `hero.abstract.ftrain-value-rows.label`: value rows after training
- `hero.abstract.ftrain-value-rows.note`: our SDM's four value tables after 20M tokens of training, every row started at zero: sorted, lit where rows grew past norm 1; 1% of rows hold 42% of table one's weight
- `hero.abstract.fwrite-bind-bundle.label`: bind and bundle
- `hero.abstract.fwrite-bind-bundle.note`: enfolding three facts: each 16-bit address bound to its value by XOR, the three summed into counters and signed into the Complicate C; unbinding C with the first address gives back 12 of its 16 bits
- `hero.abstract.fwrite-cdt-thinning.label`: thinning a bundle
- `hero.abstract.fwrite-cdt-thinning.note`: sparse binary facts of 16 bits in 256 bundled by a logical or hold 45; context-dependent thinning keeps 15, near one fact's density, with 5, 4 and 6 bits of each fact
- `hero.abstract.fwrite-counter-clip.label`: clipped counters
- `hero.abstract.fwrite-counter-clip.note`: a real SDM of 1,500 hard-locations, 128-bit words written at their own address, bit-counters clipped at 1, 3 or 7: after 720 words it reads back 68.4%, 87.5%, 92.6% of bits, unclipped 92.1%
- `hero.abstract.fwrite-counter-walks.label`: counters as walks
- `hero.abstract.fwrite-counter-walks.note`: the bit-counters of one SDM hard-location under 400 writes of random words: random walks, 95.8% ending inside 2 sqrt(T) = 40; one word written 40 times climbs out (bold)
- `hero.abstract.fwrite-shared-locations.label`: where writes land
- `hero.abstract.fwrite-shared-locations.note`: 600 hard-locations of a real SDM in 64 bits, three words written, a circle for each: each location a write reached is a dot in its circles; 319 hold none, 224 one, 55 two, 2 all three
- `hero.abstract.gabor-fields.label`: receptive fields
- `hero.abstract.gabor-fields.note`: eighteen Gabor patches, the edge detectors a sparse code of natural images learns (Olshausen and Field), much as cells in the visual cortex respond
- `hero.abstract.gaussian-mixture.label`: a mixture
- `hero.abstract.gaussian-mixture.note`: the density contours of three Gaussians
- `hero.abstract.golgi-forest.label`: a neural forest
- `hero.abstract.golgi-forest.note`: a schematic forest of neurons as a Golgi stain shows them, a few cells in a hundred, each in full; each one sums its inputs into a chance of firing, as a p-bit does
- `hero.abstract.gradient-descent.label`: gradient descent
- `hero.abstract.gradient-descent.note`: gradient steps zigzag down a narrow valley
- `hero.abstract.graph-of-pulls.label`: a graph of pulls
- `hero.abstract.graph-of-pulls.note`: lights joined to their nearest neighbours, line weight is pull
- `hero.abstract.grid-cell-map.label`: a grid cell
- `hero.abstract.grid-cell-map.note`: a modelled grid cell: a random walk around a box (the trail of small dots) and its spikes (the large dots), fired where three waves 60 degrees apart add up; a distributed code for place
- `hero.abstract.hard-locations.label`: hard locations
- `hero.abstract.hard-locations.note`: hard locations scattered in the address space; those inside the activation radius wake
- `hero.abstract.hebb-outer-product.label`: fire together
- `hero.abstract.hebb-outer-product.note`: Hebb's rule as an outer product: a link grows only where both its units are on, so one pattern of 16 units lights a plaid of links; summed over patterns, these are a Hopfield net's weights
- `hero.abstract.hex-lattice.label`: a hex lattice
- `hero.abstract.hex-lattice.note`: a hexagonal lattice with some sites occupied
- `hero.abstract.hilbert-curve.label`: a Hilbert curve
- `hero.abstract.hilbert-curve.note`: one line that visits every cell of a 16 by 16 grid, near cells kept near
- `hero.abstract.hodgkin-huxley-spikes.label`: action potentials
- `hero.abstract.hodgkin-huxley-spikes.note`: the Hodgkin-Huxley equations integrated: a steady current switched on at 5 ms makes the membrane spike 7 times in 100 ms, each spike an all-or-none bit
- `hero.abstract.hopfield-recall.label`: Hopfield recall
- `hero.abstract.hopfield-recall.note`: a Hopfield net of 256 units storing a heart, a ring and a cross: given the heart with 64 bits flipped, it settles back to the heart
- `hero.abstract.hopfield-weights.label`: Hopfield weights
- `hero.abstract.hopfield-weights.note`: the weight matrix of a Hopfield net storing three patterns: filled is a pull, a ring a push
- `hero.abstract.hypercube-shell.label`: the hypercube
- `hero.abstract.hypercube-shell.note`: a four-dimensional cube: one corner and its Hamming neighbours filled
- `hero.abstract.ising-domains.label`: Ising domains
- `hero.abstract.ising-domains.note`: the domains of a cooled Ising field, each drawn as a solid patch
- `hero.abstract.julia-set.label`: a Julia set
- `hero.abstract.julia-set.note`: the filled Julia set of z squared minus 0.8 plus 0.156i
- `hero.abstract.kfold-foldback-rings.label`: the welcome widens
- `hero.abstract.kfold-foldback-rings.note`: an SDM crowded with 1,400 words; how far away an iterated read may start and still come home to one word, as its verdict is folded back 0 to 6 times: 0, 0, 4, 44, 94, 107, 128 bits
- `hero.abstract.kfold-handshake.label`: binding as a handshake
- `hero.abstract.kfold-handshake.note`: two unitary vectors of 16 numbers as phase dials, one per frequency: binding adds the two angles on every dial (third row), and unbinding with the first gives the second back (bottom row)
- `hero.abstract.kfold-room-for-both.label`: room for both
- `hero.abstract.kfold-room-for-both.note`: one 2,048-number vector holds two half rings, each bound to its own key; unbinding with a key draws its own half (4.18 against 0.46 on the other), and together they close the ring
- `hero.abstract.kfold-two-shores.label`: two shores, one vector
- `hero.abstract.kfold-two-shores.note`: 12 items on each shore, paired, bound and summed into one 1,024-number vector; each item bound with it lands on its own partner (12 of 12, cosine at least 0.25, wrong ones at most 0.09)
- `hero.abstract.kfold-two-stores.label`: two memories made whole
- `hero.abstract.kfold-two-stores.note`: two SDMs, each shown part of a picture of two linked rings; alone each reads its own part and guesses the rest (54 and 45 bits wrong); their counters added read it whole (0 wrong)
- `hero.abstract.kmany-acquainted.label`: strangers become acquainted
- `hero.abstract.kmany-acquainted.note`: two p-bits as their coupling grows from 0 to 2.2: the exact joint table moves to its diagonal and their mutual information rises from 0 to 0.905 bits
- `hero.abstract.kmany-chord-diagonal.label`: a chord of three
- `hero.abstract.kmany-chord-diagonal.note`: three nearly orthogonal hypervectors in 10,000 dimensions summed into a chord: it sits at 54.3, 54.5 and 54.4 degrees to each, the cube's diagonal
- `hero.abstract.kmany-ring-agrees.label`: a ring comes to agree
- `hero.abstract.kmany-ring-agrees.note`: a ring of 121 p-bits at zero temperature, each taking the majority of itself and two cells on one side: this ring agrees with its first majority in 76 steps, as 88% of random rings do
- `hero.abstract.kmany-shared-part.label`: a part held by both
- `hero.abstract.kmany-shared-part.note`: a Hopfield net of 1,040 units holds two memories sharing their middle; each comes back whole from a noisy start on its own side only, the shared part held by both
- `hero.abstract.kmany-together.label`: many make one
- `hero.abstract.kmany-together.note`: an SDM read of the word: each of the 32 hard-locations it wakes alone holds on average 76% of its ink, with ghosts of other words; their majority reads it whole
- `hero.abstract.koch-snowflake.label`: Koch snowflake
- `hero.abstract.koch-snowflake.note`: a triangle whose every edge grows a smaller triangle, four times over
- `hero.abstract.kqua-anneal-gap.label`: the gentle way to agreement
- `hero.abstract.kqua-anneal-gap.note`: quantum annealing of a ring of 6 spins: its lowest energy levels above the ground state as the field gives way; the narrowest gap (0.11, at s 0.58) is marked, and at the end every spin agrees
- `hero.abstract.kqua-bell-threads.label`: a pair that always agrees
- `hero.abstract.kqua-bell-threads.note`: a Bell pair measured 22 times, both analysers turned to one shared random angle: each row alone is a fair coin (8 ones in 22), yet the pair agrees 22 of 22 times
- `hero.abstract.kqua-bloch-welcome.label`: welcomed into the group
- `hero.abstract.kqua-bloch-welcome.note`: quantum homogenisation on the Bloch sphere: a newcomer qubit meets 32 others in one shared state by partial swaps and spirals in to it (distance 1.63 to 0.231); each of them moves at most 0.30
- `hero.abstract.kqua-ghz-ring.label`: a circle that agrees
- `hero.abstract.kqua-ghz-ring.note`: 8 qubits on a circle: a Hadamard on one, then a CNOT passed from each to the next, makes one shared state; every one of 24 shots (the crown) comes out all 0 or all 1
- `hero.abstract.kqua-two-paths.label`: both paths at once
- `hero.abstract.kqua-two-paths.note`: a Mach-Zehnder interferometer: in superposition the photon takes both arms at once (probability 0.5 each), and with equal arms the halves meet in one bright port; below, that port over the phase
- `hero.abstract.krec-forgiven-wedge.label`: the forgiven wedge
- `hero.abstract.krec-forgiven-wedge.note`: a flower stored with five other pictures in an SDM of 4,000 hard-locations; a 195-degree wedge of its address unknown, and 20 of 20 reads still come home
- `hero.abstract.krec-graceful-stray.label`: a gentle stray
- `hero.abstract.krec-graceful-stray.note`: our model's address pushed further from a real context: the woken locations kept (thin) fall to 0.27, the read's cosine (thick) only to 0.66 (two unrelated reads: 0.48)
- `hero.abstract.krec-shoreline.label`: the reach of a memory
- `hero.abstract.krec-shoreline.note`: share of iterated-reads that come home by start distance, one row per memory size: the reach grows from 40 bits at 250 hard-locations to 96 at 8,000
- `hero.abstract.krec-spiral-home.label`: spirals home
- `hero.abstract.krec-spiral-home.note`: iterated-reads of an SDM drawn as spirals, each read a quarter turn, the radius its distance from the stored word: starts up to 77 bits away wind home
- `hero.abstract.krec-stray-flower.label`: a stranger answered
- `hero.abstract.krec-stray-flower.note`: our model's first hop for a real context (left) and for 64 random tokens (right): 64 locations each, soft weights summing to 33.9 and 31.7
- `hero.abstract.kset-braid.label`: threads into one cord
- `hero.abstract.kset-braid.note`: 16 Kuramoto oscillators with different natural paces, coupled at K 4.0 (critical about 1.6): their phases gather into one cord as the order r rises from 0.13 to 0.97
- `hero.abstract.kset-bridge.label`: a bridge of p-bits
- `hero.abstract.kset-bridge.note`: a chain of 12 p-bits as an arch at T 0.5: each stone sized by its exact agreement with the left bank, tanh(1/T)^k; the far bank still agrees 82.2% of the time
- `hero.abstract.kset-kolmogorov-loop.label`: every give, a take
- `hero.abstract.kset-kolmogorov-loop.note`: 6 states of a ring at their Boltzmann weights under Metropolis moves: on every edge the probability flowing one way equals the flow back (detailed balance), drawn as two equal arrows
- `hero.abstract.kset-longer-agreement.label`: agreement grows longer
- `hero.abstract.kset-longer-agreement.note`: an open chain of 64 p-bits sampled exactly at six temperatures, hot at the top: neighbours agree 56% of the time at T 8 and 98.8% at T 0.45, so the agreeing runs lengthen
- `hero.abstract.kset-two-clocks.label`: two clocks in step
- `hero.abstract.kset-two-clocks.note`: two oscillators slightly out of tune: apart, their trace tangles across the square; coupled at K 0.4 they lock 22.0 degrees apart (the Adler rule) and trace one ellipse
- `hero.abstract.layered-network.label`: a layered network
- `hero.abstract.layered-network.note`: a feed-forward network: four layers and their weights
- `hero.abstract.lissajous-3-2.label`: a Lissajous figure
- `hero.abstract.lissajous-3-2.note`: two oscillations at three to two, traced against each other
- `hero.abstract.log-spiral-field.label`: spiral arms
- `hero.abstract.log-spiral-field.note`: five logarithmic spiral arms
- `hero.abstract.logistic-bifurcation.label`: period doubling
- `hero.abstract.logistic-bifurcation.note`: the logistic map: one value splits into two, four, then chaos
- `hero.abstract.lorenz-attractor.label`: Lorenz attractor
- `hero.abstract.lorenz-attractor.note`: the Lorenz system traced for 9,000 steps: never settling, never leaving
- `hero.abstract.mandelbrot-set.label`: the Mandelbrot set
- `hero.abstract.mandelbrot-set.note`: the points whose orbit under z squared plus c stays bounded
- `hero.abstract.mcculloch-pitts.label`: a threshold unit
- `hero.abstract.mcculloch-pitts.note`: a McCulloch and Pitts unit: inputs 1, 0, 1, 1, 0 times weights 2, 1, -1, 2, 1 sum to 3, which meets the threshold 3, so it fires; a p-bit is this unit with a coin in it
- `hero.abstract.mem-capacity-knee.label`: capacity
- `hero.abstract.mem-capacity-knee.note`: a real SDM of 2,000 hard-locations, each word read from 20 bits off: all come back exact up to 30 stored words, then the votes start to drown
- `hero.abstract.mem-cleanup-funnel.label`: cleanup
- `hero.abstract.mem-cleanup-funnel.note`: cleanup memory: six noisy copies of a stored word pour into one, the clean word it keeps
- `hero.abstract.mem-dollar-coin.label`: the dollar of Mexico
- `hero.abstract.mem-dollar-coin.note`: Kanerva's riddle, what is the dollar of Mexico, is answered by binding: the peso, which is also written with a $
- `hero.abstract.mem-dollar-query.label`: ask the vectors
- `hero.abstract.mem-dollar-query.note`: Kanerva's riddle in 10,000-bit vectors: the dollar bound with the USA record and the Mexico record lands nearest the peso, similarity 0.63 against at most 0.51 for the rest
- `hero.abstract.mem-gram-matrix.label`: nearly orthogonal
- `hero.abstract.mem-gram-matrix.note`: the similarities of fifteen 4,096-bit hypervectors: random ones are near zero to each other, five noisy copies of one word light a block
- `hero.abstract.mem-holographic-plate.label`: a broken plate
- `hero.abstract.mem-holographic-plate.note`: cut away 40% of a 10,000-bit hypervector and flip 30% of what is left: it still matches itself at 0.70, the best of 999 others only 0.52
- `hero.abstract.mem-iterated-reads.label`: iterated reads
- `hero.abstract.mem-iterated-reads.note`: a real SDM holding 40 words of 256 bits: read again and again, a read-address up to 50 bits off falls to the word, further off it wanders
- `hero.abstract.mem-kanerva-crate.label`: KANERVA
- `hero.abstract.mem-kanerva-crate.note`: KANERVA, our Rust crate: it stores bit patterns in Kanerva's sparse distributed memory and reads them back from noisy read-addresses
- `hero.abstract.mem-million-mailboxes.label`: a wall of mailboxes
- `hero.abstract.mem-million-mailboxes.note`: each mailbox is a hard-location with a fixed random 256-bit address; a write raises the flag on the twelve nearest its own, wherever they hang
- `hero.abstract.mem-pattern-completion.label`: half a house
- `hero.abstract.mem-pattern-completion.note`: an SDM storing four little pictures is read with the right half of the house gone, and its memory gives back the whole house
- `hero.abstract.mem-permute-sequence.label`: permutation
- `hero.abstract.mem-permute-sequence.note`: one hypervector rotated a step at a time: each rotation is nearly orthogonal to the last, so it can mark a place in a sequence
- `hero.abstract.mem-phasor-binding.label`: phasor binding
- `hero.abstract.mem-phasor-binding.note`: hypervectors of phases: binding adds the angles, dial by dial, and the bottom row is the top two bound
- `hero.abstract.mem-read-pool.label`: the read vote
- `hero.abstract.mem-read-pool.note`: a read in a real SDM: the bit-counters of five woken hard-locations are summed column by column, and the sign of each sum is the bit read
- `hero.abstract.mem-role-filler-tree.label`: a record
- `hero.abstract.mem-role-filler-tree.note`: three roles each bound to a filler, then bundled by majority into one record vector that holds all three pairs
- `hero.abstract.mem-sdm-network.label`: the SDM as a network
